correctness.rationale: A finite near-norm block has infinitely many pairwise disjoint simultaneous right translates. Schatten block-sum identities make their span an exact l_p/c0 copy on which the multiplier is bounded below by an arbitrarily near-norm constant. This gives the Bernstein and strict-singularity-distance bounds; finite-codimension intersection gives Gelfand numbers; escaping rectangular compressions against finite-dimensional targets give Kolmogorov numbers and Hausdorff noncompactness. All matching upper bounds are the operator norm.

originality.rationale: Targeted searches and inspection of classical Schur-multiplier, compact Schur-multiplier, elementary-multiplier s-number, and relative Toeplitz-Schur transference literature did not locate the simultaneous flat a_n/c_n/d_n/b_n theorem or norm distance to the strictly singular class. Hladnik (2000) was not fully inspected and remains a documented residual risk.

value.rationale: The result gives a class-wide rigidity statement at every finite-dimensional approximation scale: inside relative Toeplitz Schur multipliers on Schatten classes, every nonzero operator is maximally noncompact and norm-separated from compact, finitely strictly singular, and strictly singular operators.
